pageNotes.zht: 古代常以居處代指其人。太子多居宮城東側，是為東宮；太后居所之宮名，亦為太后代稱。
pageNotes.zhs: 古代常以居处代指其人。太子多居宫城东侧，是为东宫；太后居所之宫名，亦为太后代称。
pageNotes.en: In ancient China, a person's residence often served as a metonym for the person. The Crown Prince typically resided in the eastern part of the palace complex, and was thus known as the Eastern Palace; similarly, the Empress Dowager was often referred to by the name of her residence.

pageNotes.zht: 後宮為后妃居所之統稱，即所謂「前朝後寢」。
pageNotes.zhs: 后宫为后妃居所之统称，即所谓“前朝后寝”。
pageNotes.en: The Rear Palace collectively refers to the residences of the empress and consorts, reflecting the principle of 'court in front, living quarters behind.'

notes.zht: 太子于二傅執弟子禮，皆為書不曰令，少傅稱臣，而太傅不臣。二傅與尚書東曹並選太子諸侯官屬
notes.zhs: 太子于二傅执弟子礼，皆为书不曰令，少傅称臣，而太傅不臣。二傅与尚书东曹并选太子诸侯官属
notes.en: The Crown Prince observed the etiquette of a student toward the two Tutors, and when the tutors issued instructions, they were expressed as written requests rather than orders. The Junior Tutor would refer to himself as 'subject,' but the Grand Tutor would not. The two tutors and the Imperial Secretariat Eastern Section officials together selected various subordinate officials of the Crown Prince and Marquises
